pr_title: Limit the number of http headers when receiving the http response
pr_body:
Change introduces a default limit on HTTP headers we expect to receive from server to 256. If limit is exceeded http client library indicates HTTP_R_RESPONSE_TOO_MANY_HDRLINES error. Application can use OSSL_HTTP_REQ_CTX_set_max_response_hdr_lines() to change default. Setting limit to 0 implies no limit (current behavior).

Fixes #22264

issue_context.title: Limit the number of http headers when receiving the http response
issue_context.body:
Currently the http server can push infinite number of headers and the processing of them in http_client.c will never stop.

This is not a security issue according to our policy as it is not really useful for DoS attack purposes as the http server has to keep a connection open.
comments: @DDvO might be interested in fixing this issue.
Any (type of) server could also send regular responses (http body etc.) of 'infinite' length.

If a client wants to be immune on anything like this, limits need to be configurable with sensible defaults,
such that an application that wants to handle unusually large input is not limited by the (http) client component.
I'm not sure if this topic is worth special support.
**OTC: Do we need to limit the number of HTTP headers processed on response or just keep the code as is?**
**OTC: This is not a security issue however we should limit the number processed headers to some reasonably high number for hardening.**

review_comments:
It should better have been made clear in a comment why an error is expected in case `limit == 1`:
the server response has 4 header lines (one each for the HTTP version, keep-alive, content-type, and content-length).
I wonder if adding this call isn't an overkill. If the limit was set to 1024 for example, would any application really need to override it?

I've been bitten by this a few times now.  Because you are exposing a new api call here, you need to run make update, and commit the changes to http_err.c, httperr.h and libcrypto.num.  Without that the new api call or error enumeration doesn't get exported in libcrypto, and you get the undefined symbol error here:
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/actions/runs/8203307742/job/22435829890?pr=23781

The needed additions to `http_err.c`, `httperr.h`, and BTW also to `crypto/err/openssl.txt`
are independent of any newly added API function.
If they are not added, ideally using `make errors`, already the local build fails, so one gets early feedback (also without `make update`) if not done yet.
Where does this mem bio get freed?

If I understand `OSSL_HTTP_REQ_CTX(3)` manpage correct, then I'm not supposed to free `mem` here.  Quoting from `RETURN VALUES` section of the manpage:

```
       OSSL_HTTP_REQ_CTX_exchange() and OSSL_HTTP_REQ_CTX_get0_mem_bio()
       return a pointer to a BIO on success as described above or NULL on
       failure.  The returned BIO must not be freed by the caller.
```

Why did you set `mock_args.content_type` twice?

(BTW, `mock_args.keep_alive` is already initialised suitably, so fine not to assign to that here.)
